Model-4 improves held-out NRMSE by ~93.7% over baseline (0.0039 vs 0.0622), showing the velocity loss depends on position, not unsigned quadratic drag.

Sparse projectile with quadratic drag: constant 1 coefficient is gravitational/bias acceleration, abs(v)*v coefficient is quadratic drag per unit mass (1/length). Unsigned v**2 in baseline cannot oppose motion in both directions; signed abs(v)*v does. 2-term model improves held-out NRMSE 86% and beats baseline BIC (-65.6 vs -64.8), so extra q,v terms were overfit.

Model replaces wrong unsigned v**2 drag with position-dependent damping q*v: q'' = c0 + k*q + c*v + beta*q*v. c0 is gravity/bias accel, k linear stiffness, c viscous damping per unit mass, beta gradient of damping with displacement (variable-orifice / geometry-dependent damping). Held NRMSE improves 93.6% over baseline (0.0039 vs 0.062), showing residual scaled with q*v not v^2.

Baseline v**2 cannot change sign with v, so it biases one direction; directed abs(v)*v fixes this, cutting held-out NRMSE by ~33% (0.73->0.49).
